requirement:
The `instructions` field supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result` MUST contain the following text.

```text
Before submitting your assessment, close every delivered search with finish_search({search_id, used:[tags]}). Submission fails while any search remains open. Include a tag only when you used information in its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read. Entries whose source you subsequently read with habeas may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including for an empty search. finish_search records dependencies and does not request more source.
```
rationale:
**Obligation.** The subject has one obligation. The `instructions` field on the first delivered search result MUST contain the quoted text. When the field appears is the job of `first_result`, which has its own tests.

**How the expected text is derived.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[approved_text]` takes the first ```` ```text ```` block of requirement `search_accounting.instructions` straight from `md/requirements/authoring.md` through `include_str!`. The tests therefore compare against the requirement's own text, not against a copy that could drift. The result renderer in `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[Listing]/fn[render]` uses the same helper. I checked this with a search and did not read the whole function. The comparison therefore holds only while the book text is the single source of truth. That is what the requirement describes, so I don't count it as a gap.

**Tests that cover it.**
- `src/authoring/searches.rs#mod[tests]/fn[delivered_searches_including_empty_results_need_explicit_completion]`:
  - It asserts that the first `ripgrep` result with matches has `instructions` equal to the approved text.
  - It runs an empty-result `ripgrep` search and an empty-result `ast_grep` search, each on a fresh `ResultPages`. Each asserts `matches == []` and `instructions` equal to the approved text. This covers the no-matches case and both tools.
  - It dispatches a failing `ripgrep` pattern first, and the first delivered result still carries the instructions.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_pages_are_accounted_only_when_delivered_and_replay_stays_closed]` runs paged `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` searches. For each, it asserts that the first result's `instructions` equal the approved text.

Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. The assertions are full-string equality, so a missing, truncated or altered instruction would fail them. Absence of the field on later results and continuation pages belongs to `first_result`, not to this subject.

I found no gap.

text: The `instructions` field supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result` MUST contain the following text.

Before submitting your assessment, close every delivered search with finish_search({search_id, used:[tags]}). Submission fails while any search remains open. Include a tag only when you used information in its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read. Entries whose source you subsequently read with habeas may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including for an empty search. finish_search records dependencies and does not request more source.
Each assessment MUST include `instructions` on its first delivered search
result, even when the result has no matches. `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` share
this rule. A failed search leaves the instructions for the first delivered
result. Subsequent searches and continuation pages MUST omit the field.
